newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine's Kuchma urges reappointment of cbank head.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine's Kuchma urges reappointment of cbank head.

text.p: President Leonid Kuchma has urged parliament to award acting central bank chief Viktor Yushchenko a second term, Kuchma's press service said on Tuesday.

"The president thinks replacing the national bank chief in the current situation could have a negative effect on the condition and functioning of the state's financial system," the press service said in a statement.
Kuchma met leaders of parliamentary parties and groups late on Monday to urge them to back Yushchenko, who is a strong advocate of tough monetary reform.
Yushchenko's first, four-year term expired on January 26, but deputies appointed him acting head of the bank until February 5 to give them time to vote on his reappointment.
Yushchenko already has support from Kuchma and the cabinet and needs a majority of 226 deputies to win another term.
Prime Minister Pavlo Lazarenko, who enjoys broad support among conservative leftists in parliament, has voiced support for Yushchenko despite having criticised Yushchenko's policies in the past.
Economists credit Yushchenko with cutting inflation to 39.7 percent last year from 181.7 percent in 1995.
